questions: Can we move stones from bag B to bag A, or only from A to B as written? The operation says 'choose two bags A and B, and move stones from bag A into bag B' – does the order of naming matter, i.e., is the first chosen bag always the source and the second the destination?
Is the operation allowed to move zero stones (i.e., do nothing) between bags, and does that count as performing the operation?
Are we allowed to move stones from a bag to itself? The description says 'choose two bags A and B' – if A and B can be the same bag, moving stones within the same bag would be a no-op.
Must we move a positive integer number of stones each time, or can we move a fractional number of stones?
Does the operation require that bag A has at least one stone before moving, i.e., can we attempt to move from an empty bag?
Is there any limit on how many stones can be moved in a single operation (e.g., all stones from bag A, or only some subset)?
Can we perform the operation an infinite number of times in theory, or is there an implicit bound due to finite stones?

Are the bags distinguishable for the purpose of counting different possible XOR values? That is, if two final configurations have the same multiset of stone counts but assigned to different bags, do they produce the same XOR value?
